Children and the step of the supplied proof each one covers:
- coeff_bounds (fact (F1) and the coefficient comparison in step 4). For the Euclidean coefficient norm: |α(e_I)| ≤ |α| for strictly increasing I, and Σ_i α(e_{ι∘i.succAbove})² ≤ |α|². It is used by divergence_field and by the parent's mass bound.
- divergence_field (the three bullets of step 4). Take a C^∞ m-form γ, a strictly increasing ι and any base point a. Then there is a C^∞ field G with |G(y)| ≤ |γ(Φ y)| and trace DG(y) = dγ(Φ y)(E).
- current_exists (steps 1–2). This is (I) and (II), with no monotonicity assumed on ι.
- support_faces (step 5). This is (III)(c), with no monotonicity assumed on ι.

The parent then proves its frozen type as follows.
1. (I) and (II) come from current_exists, and (III)(c) from support_faces.
2. (III)(a), mass bound (supplied step 3).
   - Unfold GeometricCurrentOn.mass and massOn, then apply sSup_le over massAdmissibleOn univ (m+1) univ and ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal.
   - Rewrite D ω by the formula and bound it by Σ_p |∫ w_p h_p|.
   - Each term satisfies |∫ w_p h_p| ≤ ∫|w_p|. This is norm_integral_le_of_norm_le with the majorant |w_p|, using |ω(Φ_p y)(E_p)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(Φ_p y)) ≤ 1. That inequality is coeff_bounds (i) with I = p.1 plus admissibility.
3. (III)(b), boundary-mass bound (supplied step 4).
   - Take the same supremum over admissible γ. GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply and the formula give D.boundary γ = Σ_p ∫ w_p · (exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m γ)(Φ_p y)(E_p).
   - For each p ∈ s, apply divergence_field to γ, with ι := p.1, a := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) and the smoothness proof γ.property.1.1. It gives G_p with ‖G_p y‖ ≤ 1 (admissibility).
   - The integrand equals w_p · trace(fderiv G_p y) pointwise. Prove this with funext, rewriting by the trace identity, and rfl: the coercion of exteriorDerivativeTestOn is exteriorDerivative by definition.
   - The hypothesis on B then bounds the p-th term by B_p.

subproblems.title: Coefficient bounds for the Euclidean covector norm (Simon 6.1.15)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let α be a k-covector on ℝ^P (α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) k, a continuous alternating k-linear form). Write e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 (l ∈ Fin P) for the standard basis of ℝ^P, e_J := (e_{J(0)}, …, e_{J(k−1)}) for J : Fin k → Fin P, and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{J : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_J)²)^{1/2}. Then: (i) |α(e_I)| ≤ |α| for every strictly increasing I : Fin k → Fin P; (ii) for every strictly increasing ι : Fin (k+1) → Fin P, Σ_{i ∈ Fin (k+1)} α(e_{ι(i.succAbove 0)}, …, e_{ι(i.succAbove (k−1))})² ≤ |α|², where i.succAbove : Fin k → Fin (k+1) is the increasing enumeration of Fin (k+1) ∖ {i}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) k), (∀ I : Fin k → Fin P, StrictMono I → |α (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (I j) (1 : ℝ))| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ ∀ ι : Fin (k + 1) → Fin P, StrictMono ι → ∑ i : Fin (k + 1), (α (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι (i.succAbove j)) (1 : ℝ))) ^ 2 ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 5.1, displays (29)–(30) and (34) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1862–1906), as written out in the parent-supplied proof of cmcdtfr_face_integral_current (its facts (F1)–(F2) and steps 1–5). This child is fact (F1) of that proof, together with the coefficient comparison in the second bullet of its step 4.
1. Notation. For J : Fin k → Fin P let f(J) := α(e_J)² if J is strictly increasing and f(J) := 0 otherwise. Since EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ l = EuclideanSpace.single l 1 = e_l (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply), the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm reads |α| = √S with S := Σ_{J : Fin k → Fin P} f(J) (sum over the finite type of all maps Fin k → Fin P). Each f(J) is a square or 0, so f(J) ≥ 0, S ≥ 0 and |α|² = S (Real.sq_sqrt).
2. Proof of (i). Let I be strictly increasing. Then f(I) = α(e_I)². All terms of S are nonnegative, so the single term f(I) is at most the whole sum (Finset.single_le_sum): α(e_I)² ≤ S. Hence |α(e_I)| ≤ √S = |α| (Real.abs_le_sqrt).
3. Proof of (ii), the faces are strictly increasing. Let ι : Fin (k+1) → Fin P be strictly increasing and, for i ∈ Fin (k+1), put J_i := ι ∘ i.succAbove : Fin k → Fin P. The map i.succAbove is strictly increasing (Fin.strictMono_succAbove), so J_i is strictly increasing as a composition of strictly increasing maps. Therefore f(J_i) = α(e_{J_i})² = α(e_{ι(i.succAbove 0)}, …, e_{ι(i.succAbove (k−1))})², which is the i-th summand on the left side of (ii).
4. The faces are pairwise distinct. Suppose J_i = J_{i'}. Then ι(i.succAbove j) = ι(i'.succAbove j) for every j ∈ Fin k; ι is injective (StrictMono.injective), so i.succAbove = i'.succAbove as functions, and therefore i = i' (Fin.succAbove_left_injective). So i ↦ J_i is injective.
5. Comparison. Let T ⊆ (Fin k → Fin P) be the image of Fin (k+1) under i ↦ J_i. By steps 3–4 and Finset.sum_image, Σ_i α(e_{J_i})² = Σ_i f(J_i) = Σ_{J ∈ T} f(J). Since T is a subset of all maps and f ≥ 0, Σ_{J ∈ T} f(J) ≤ Σ_J f(J) = S = |α|² (Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg). This is (ii). ∎
proof_key_steps: |α|² = S := Σ_J f(J) with f(J) = α(e_J)² on strictly increasing J and 0 otherwise (basisFun_apply), all terms ≥ 0.
(i): the single term f(I) ≤ S, then |α(e_I)| ≤ √S by Real.abs_le_sqrt.
(ii): J_i = ι ∘ i.succAbove is strictly increasing and i ↦ J_i is injective (ι injective, succAbove_left_injective).
(ii): Σ_i f(J_i) is the sub-sum of S over the image of i ↦ J_i, hence ≤ S = |α|².

subproblems.title: The face pull-back of dγ is the divergence of a smooth field bounded by |γ|
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let γ be a C^∞ differential m-form on ℝ^P (γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m with ContDiff ℝ ∞ γ, order ∞ = ↑(⊤ : ℕ∞), not analytic), let ι : Fin n → Fin P be strictly increasing and a ∈ ℝ^P. Write e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 ∈ ℝ^P, Φ(y) := a + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} for y ∈ ℝⁿ (= Euclid n), and E := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}). Then there is a C^∞ map G : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ such that for every y ∈ ℝⁿ: (a) |G(y)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm(γ(Φ(y))) (Euclidean norm of G(y)), and (b) trace DG(y) = (dγ)(Φ(y))(E), where DG(y) = fderiv ℝ G y, trace is LinearMap.trace on ℝⁿ and dγ = exteriorDerivative γ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) (ι : Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) (a : Euclid P), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) γ → StrictMono ι → ∃ G : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) G ∧ (∀ y, ‖G y‖ ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm (γ (a + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)))) ∧ ∀ y, LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ G y) = exteriorDerivative γ (a + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 5.1, displays (29)–(30) and (34) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1862–1906), as written out in the parent-supplied proof of cmcdtfr_face_integral_current (its facts (F1)–(F2) and steps 1–5). This child is the construction of the vector field G_p in step 4 of that proof (its three bullets), stated for an arbitrary base point a and an arbitrary smooth form γ; it uses the sibling coeff_bounds (ii).
1. The affine map. Let b_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 ∈ ℝⁿ (the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun of ℝⁿ) and let L : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be the continuous linear map L(y) := Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} (for instance L = Σ_j (EuclideanSpace.proj j).smulRight e_{ι(j)}). Then Φ = a + L, so Φ is C^∞ and HasFDerivAt Φ L y for every y. Moreover L(b_i) = Σ_j (b_i)_j e_{ι(j)} = e_{ι(i)}, since (b_i)_j = 1 if j = i and 0 otherwise.
2. The coordinate functions. For i ∈ Fin n put E^(i) := i.removeNth E, i.e. E^(i)_j = E(i.succAbove j) = e_{ι(i.succAbove j)} for j ∈ Fin m (Fin.removeNth unfolds definitionally to this), and g_i(x) := γ(x)(E^(i)) for x ∈ ℝ^P. Evaluation at the fixed tuple E^(i) is a continuous linear map on m-covectors (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ E^(i)), so g_i is the composition of a continuous linear map with the C^∞ map γ and is C^∞; in particular g_i is differentiable everywhere and Dg_i(x) = fderiv ℝ (fun x => γ x (i.removeNth E)) x, the derivative occurring in exteriorDerivative_apply.
3. Definition of G. G(y) := toLp(i ↦ (−1)^i g_i(Φ(y))) ∈ ℝⁿ; its i-th coordinate is G_i(y) = (−1)^i g_i(Φ(y)).
4. G is C^∞. A map into ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is C^∞ iff every coordinate is (contDiff_euclidean). Each G_i = (−1)^i · (g_i ∘ Φ) is a constant times a composition of C^∞ maps (steps 1–2), hence C^∞. So G is C^∞.
5. Bound (a). Fix y and put α := γ(Φ(y)) ∈ Covector (Euclid P) m. By EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, |G(y)| = √(Σ_i |G_i(y)|²), and |G_i(y)|² = ((−1)^i)² g_i(Φ y)² = α(E^(i))² = α(e_{ι(i.succAbove 0)}, …, e_{ι(i.succAbove (m−1))})², because ((−1)^i)² = 1. By coeff_bounds (ii), applied with k := m to this α and to the strictly increasing ι : Fin (m+1) → Fin P, Σ_i α(E^(i))² ≤ |α|² with |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α ≥ 0. Taking square roots (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt, then Real.sqrt_sq) gives |G(y)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm(γ(Φ(y))).
6. The trace as a sum of diagonal entries. For a linear map A of ℝⁿ, trace A = Σ_i ⟨b_i, A b_i⟩ (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner with the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun, whose i-th vector is b_i by EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply), and ⟨b_i, v⟩ = v_i (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left). Hence trace DG(y) = Σ_i (DG(y) b_i)_i.
7. The diagonal entries. G is differentiable at y (step 4). The coordinate map v ↦ v_i is continuous linear (PiLp.proj), so composing (PiLp.hasFDerivAt_apply) with HasFDerivAt G (DG(y)) y shows that y ↦ G_i(y) has derivative v ↦ (DG(y) v)_i at y; by uniqueness of the derivative, (DG(y) b_i)_i = D(G_i)(y)(b_i). By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp with step 1, then multiplication by the constant (−1)^i), D(G_i)(y) = (−1)^i · (Dg_i(Φ(y)) ∘ L). Therefore (DG(y) b_i)_i = (−1)^i Dg_i(Φ(y))(L b_i) = (−1)^i Dg_i(Φ(y))(e_{ι(i)}).
8. The exterior derivative. γ is differentiable at Φ(y) (C^∞), so by exteriorDerivative_apply (SimonGMT, Chapter06/Forms.lean) with v := E, dγ(Φ(y))(E) = Σ_i (−1 : ℤ)^i • fderiv ℝ (fun x => γ x (i.removeNth E)) (Φ(y)) (E i) = Σ_i (−1)^i Dg_i(Φ(y))(e_{ι(i)}), since E i = e_{ι(i)} and the integer power acts on ℝ by (−1 : ℤ)^i • r = (−1)^i r (zsmul_eq_mul).
9. Conclusion. By steps 6–8, trace DG(y) = Σ_i (−1)^i Dg_i(Φ(y))(e_{ι(i)}) = dγ(Φ(y))(E) for every y, which is (b). Together with steps 4 and 5, G is a C^∞ map with properties (a) and (b). ∎
proof_key_steps: Φ = a + L with L(y) = Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} continuous linear, DΦ ≡ L and L(b_i) = e_{ι(i)}.
g_i(x) := γ(x)(i.removeNth E) is C^∞ (evaluation at a fixed tuple is continuous linear); G_i(y) := (−1)^i g_i(Φ(y)) gives C^∞ G.
|G(y)|² = Σ_i γ(Φ y)(e_{ι∘i.succAbove})² ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm(γ(Φ y))² by coeff_bounds (ii).
trace DG(y) = Σ_i (DG(y)b_i)_i = Σ_i (−1)^i Dg_i(Φ y)(e_{ι(i)}) by trace_eq_sum_inner, coordinate projection and the chain rule.
exteriorDerivative_apply gives dγ(Φ y)(E) = Σ_i (−1)^i Dg_i(Φ y)(e_{ι(i)}), so trace DG(y) = dγ(Φ y)(E).

subproblems.title: Integrable densities on finitely many faces define a current
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let s be a finite set of pairs p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin n → Fin P (arbitrary; no monotonicity is needed) and b : Fin P → ℤ, and let w : (pairs) → ℝⁿ → ℝ be such that w_p is Lebesgue integrable on Q₁ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : 0 < y_i < 1 ∀ i} for every p ∈ s (ℝⁿ = Euclid n with volume). Write e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1, Φ_p(y) := toLp(b) + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} ∈ ℝ^P and E_p := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}). Then: (I) for every test n-form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (ω : TestFormOn univ n, a C^∞ compactly supported n-form) and every p ∈ s, the function y ↦ w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p) is integrable on Q₁; (II) there is a current D ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) with D(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p) dy for every test n-form ω.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (s : Finset ((Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ))) (w : (Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), (∀ p ∈ s, IntegrableOn (w p) {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), ∀ p ∈ s, IntegrableOn (fun y => w p y * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ))) {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}) ∧ ∃ D : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), D ω = ∑ p ∈ s, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, w p y * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 5.1, displays (29)–(30) and (34) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1862–1906), as written out in the parent-supplied proof of cmcdtfr_face_integral_current (its facts (F1)–(F2) and steps 1–5). This child is steps 1 (I) and 2 (II) of that proof, using its fact (F2). The operator-norm bound |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖ of (F1) is used, so no monotonicity of ι is needed.
1. Continuity. Put h_{p,ω}(y) := ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p). The map Φ_p is continuous: it is a constant plus the finite sum of the maps y ↦ y_j e_{ι(j)}, and each coordinate y ↦ y_j is continuous (PiLp.continuous_apply). Evaluation at the fixed tuple E_p is a continuous linear map on covectors (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply), and ω is continuous because it is C^∞. So h_{p,ω} is continuous, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for volume restricted to Q₁.
2. Pointwise bound. For every x, |ω(x)(E_p)| ≤ ‖ω(x)‖·Π_j ‖e_{ι(j)}‖ = ‖ω(x)‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; ‖e_l‖ = 1 by PiLp.norm_single), where ‖ω(x)‖ is the operator norm. Since ω is continuous with compact support, there is C ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ C for all x (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous). Hence |h_{p,ω}(y)| ≤ C for all y.
3. Proof of (I). For p ∈ s, w_p is integrable on Q₁ and h_{p,ω} is a.e.-strongly measurable with |h_{p,ω}| ≤ C. So the product y ↦ w_p(y)·h_{p,ω}(y) is integrable on Q₁ (Integrable.mul_bdd).
4. Linearity. For ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n set L(ω) := Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y)·h_{p,ω}(y) dy. The coercion of ω + η to a form is the pointwise sum and covectors are additive, so h_{p,ω+η} = h_{p,ω} + h_{p,η}; by (I) both products are integrable on Q₁, so ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω+η} = ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω} + ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,η} (integral_add), and summing over p ∈ s (Finset.sum_add_distrib) gives L(ω + η) = L(ω) + L(η). Likewise h_{p,cω} = c·h_{p,ω}, so ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,cω} = c·∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω} (integral_const_mul) and L(cω) = c·L(ω) (Finset.mul_sum). Thus L is an ℝ-linear map TestFormOn univ n → ℝ.
5. Uniform estimate. Let A := Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} |w_p| ≥ 0. Let δ ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ δ for all x. By step 2, |w_p(y) h_{p,ω}(y)| ≤ |w_p(y)|·δ for all y, and y ↦ |w_p(y)|·δ is integrable on Q₁. Hence |∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω}| ≤ ∫_{Q₁} |w_p|·δ = δ ∫_{Q₁} |w_p| (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, integral_mul_const), and |L(ω)| ≤ Σ_{p∈s} |∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω}| ≤ A·δ (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs).
6. Sequential continuity. Let (ω_j) be a sequence of test forms with TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0. Then there is a compact K with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j and, for each order k, iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k 0 uniformly on K. Take k = 0. The coercion of the zero test form is the zero form, whose 0-th iterated derivative is 0, and ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x‖ = ‖ω_j(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero). Let ε > 0 and δ := ε/(A + 1) > 0. By uniform convergence (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff) there is N such that ‖ω_j(x)‖ < δ for all j ≥ N and x ∈ K. If x ∉ K then x ∉ tsupport ω_j, so ω_j(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Hence ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ δ for all x and all j ≥ N, and by step 5, |L(ω_j)| ≤ A·ε/(A + 1) < ε for j ≥ N. So L(ω_j) → 0.
7. Conclusion. The pair ⟨L, step 6⟩ is an element D of GeometricCurrentOn univ n (a linear map on TestFormOn univ n with the sequential continuity of the structure). By construction D(ω) = L(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p) dy for every ω (definitional). With (I) from step 3 this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: h_{p,ω}(y) = ω(Φ_p y)(E_p) is continuous and |h_{p,ω}| ≤ ‖ω(·)‖ ≤ C (le_opNorm, unit basis vectors, compact support).
(I): w_p·h_{p,ω} is integrable on Q₁ by Integrable.mul_bdd.
L(ω) := Σ_p ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω} is linear by integral_add / integral_const_mul, using (I).
Order-0 uniform convergence on the common compact K and vanishing off K give L(ω_j) → 0, so ⟨L, cont⟩ is the required D.

subproblems.title: The support of a face current lies on the faces with nonzero density
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let s be a finite set of pairs p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin n → Fin P (arbitrary) and b : Fin P → ℤ, and let w_p : ℝⁿ → ℝ be integrable on Q₁ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : 0 < y_i < 1 ∀ i} for every p ∈ s. Write Φ_p(y) := toLp(b) + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} and E_p := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}) with e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1. Let D ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) satisfy D(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p) dy for every test n-form ω. Then every x ∈ spt D (D.support = univ ∖ zeroRegion D, Simon 6.2.11) equals Φ_p(y) for some p ∈ s with ∫_{Q₁} |w_p| ≠ 0 and some y ∈ [0,1]ⁿ (0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for all i).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (s : Finset ((Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ))) (w : (Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (D : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), (∀ p ∈ s, IntegrableOn (w p) {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), D ω = ∑ p ∈ s, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, w p y * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ))) → ∀ x ∈ D.support, ∃ p ∈ s, (∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |w p y|) ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ y : Euclid (m + 1), (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) ∧ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) = x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 5.1, displays (29)–(30) and (34) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1862–1906), as written out in the parent-supplied proof of cmcdtfr_face_integral_current (its facts (F1)–(F2) and steps 1–5). This child is step 5 of that proof.
1. Setup by contradiction. Let x ∈ spt D and suppose that x ≠ Φ_p(y) for every p ∈ s with ∫_{Q₁}|w_p| ≠ 0 and every y ∈ Cⁿ := {y : 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 ∀ i}. Put s* := {p ∈ s : ∫_{Q₁}|w_p| ≠ 0} and Z := ⋃_{p∈s*} Φ_p(Cⁿ). The assumption says exactly x ∉ Z.
2. Z is compact. Cⁿ is compact: under the homeomorphism ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) ≅ (Fin n → ℝ) (PiLp.homeomorph) it is the preimage of the product Π_i [0,1], which is compact (isCompact_univ_pi, isCompact_Icc). Each Φ_p is continuous (a constant plus a finite sum of y ↦ y_j e_{ι(j)}), so Φ_p(Cⁿ) is compact (IsCompact.image), and the finite union Z is compact (Finset.isCompact_biUnion). Hence Z is closed, ℝ^P ∖ Z is open and contains x, and there is r > 0 with ball(x, r) ∩ Z = ∅ (Metric.isOpen_iff).
3. The ball is admissible for the zero region. W := ball(x, r) is open; its closure is contained in closedBall(x, r) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall), which is compact because ℝ^P is a proper space (isCompact_closedBall); so closure W is a closed subset of a compact set and is compact. Trivially closure W ⊆ univ.
4. D vanishes on W. Let ω be a test n-form with tsupport ω ⊆ W. By hypothesis D(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} I_p with I_p := ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p) dy; we show I_p = 0 for every p ∈ s (Finset.sum_eq_zero).
(a) If ∫_{Q₁}|w_p| = 0: the function |w_p| is nonnegative and integrable on Q₁ (w_p is), so its zero integral forces |w_p| = 0 almost everywhere on Q₁ (integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg for volume restricted to Q₁). Then the integrand w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p y)(E_p) vanishes for a.e. y ∈ Q₁, and I_p = 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae).
(b) If ∫_{Q₁}|w_p| ≠ 0, then p ∈ s*. For y ∈ Q₁ we have 0 < y_i < 1, hence y ∈ Cⁿ and Φ_p(y) ∈ Z. Since W ∩ Z = ∅ and tsupport ω ⊆ W, Φ_p(y) ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(Φ_p(y)) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and the integrand is 0 at every y ∈ Q₁. Hence I_p = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero).
Thus D(ω) = 0 for every such ω, i.e. D vanishes on W (GeometricCurrentOn.VanishesOn).
5. Contradiction. By steps 3–4, W is one of the open sets with compact closure contained in univ on which D vanishes, and x ∈ W; so x ∈ zeroRegion D. But x ∈ spt D = univ ∖ zeroRegion D. This contradiction shows that there are p ∈ s with ∫_{Q₁}|w_p| ≠ 0 and y ∈ Cⁿ with Φ_p(y) = x. ∎
proof_key_steps: Z is compact (compact cube, continuous Φ_p, finite union), hence closed; pick ball(x, r) disjoint from Z, whose closure is compact.
Faces with ∫_{Q₁}|w_p| = 0 contribute 0 since w_p = 0 a.e. on Q₁; faces in s* map Q₁ into Z, where every test form supported in the ball vanishes.
So D vanishes on the ball, x ∈ zeroRegion D, contradicting x ∈ spt D.
